verifiedRecords.graph: Undirected labeled graphs, degree at most Δ. Positive edge weights normalized to maximum 1; n, Δ, ε and the maximum weight are supplied. Theorem 24 states w_min(ε)<1. Weights are available with adjacency entries (or O(1) weight reads).
verifiedRecords.theorem: EMR arXiv v3, Theorem 24; Sections 2.2 and 8.1–8.2; Algorithms 8–10.
verifiedRecords.notes: Explicit atlas conversion: the source probe returns the reverse port. Recovering it by scanning the returned neighbor costs at most Δ ordinary indexed-neighbor probes. To return the mate of v, inspect its at most Δ incident edges with the consistent edge-membership oracle. Thus a source cost Q gives O(Δ²(Q+1)) ordinary probes per mate query. These are probes, not distributed LOCAL rounds or CPU time. Source Q=(1/w_min(ε))^{Δ^{O(1/ε)}}(log* n)^{O(ε⁻¹ log(1/ε))}. Here w_min(ε)=min{w(e):w(e)≥ε/n} after normalization, following the source notation and its rounding argument. Do not suppress this dependence when tiny weights are allowed. This upper row covers the source’s w_min(ε)<1 regime; the equal-weight case is separately shown below. For fixed Δ, ε and a constant positive weight floor, the n dependence is polynomial in log* n. No global weight-estimation claim is included. This bound need not be sublinear for every parameter regime.

verifiedRecords.graph: Undirected labeled graphs of maximum degree Δ with every edge weight equal to 1; n, Δ and ε supplied. The unit-weight problem is maximum cardinality matching.
verifiedRecords.theorem: EMR arXiv v3, Theorem 17 and Section 2.2; Algorithm 4.
verifiedRecords.notes: Explicit atlas conversion: the source probe returns the reverse port. Recovering it by scanning the returned neighbor costs at most Δ ordinary indexed-neighbor probes. To return the mate of v, inspect its at most Δ incident edges with the consistent edge-membership oracle. Thus a source cost Q gives O(Δ²(Q+1)) ordinary probes per mate query. These are probes, not distributed LOCAL rounds or CPU time. Theorem 17 states Q=(log* n)^{⌈1/ε⌉+1}·2^{Δ^{O(1/ε)}} for deterministic stateless edge membership. Unit weights turn the cardinality guarantee into the identical total-weight guarantee. This is a compatible baseline beside the unit-weight lower bound; it is not claimed to be the fastest cardinality LCA.

verifiedRecords.graph: Bipartite hard instances with all edge weights 1; 0<ε≤0.01 and log⁴ n≤Δ≤n^ε. This is not a bound for fixed Δ as n tends to infinity.
verifiedRecords.theorem: BRR arXiv v1, Theorem 1, Remark 1 and Introduction: The LCA Model.
verifiedRecords.notes: Explicit unit-weight transfer: w(M)=|M| and OPT_w=OPT≤n/2. A (1−ε)-multiplicative weighted matching therefore also satisfies |M|≥OPT−εn. Theorem 1 rules out fewer than Δ^{Ω(1/ε)} ordinary adjacency-list probes per mate query in its stated degree window. The source already requests the mate or unmatched, so there is no edge-output conversion in this lower bound. It remains valid without query-order obliviousness. This is not a lower bound on weight-range dependence or on fixed-degree n dependence.

coverageNote: Verified deterministic weighted LCA baseline plus an explicitly compatible unit-weight comparison. These records do not claim exhaustive coverage or weight-range optimality. Global optimum-weight estimation is a separate task and is not plotted.
lowerBoundStatus: BRR Theorem 1 transfers on unit weights only; its growing-degree window is shown. No weighted-specific lower bound on the weight ratio is claimed.
axisNote: Symbolic theorem formulas; row order and spacing do not order mixed functions of n, Δ, ε and the minimum weight.
